title: Python for Data
audience: Python learners preparing for data and ML work
promise: Turn raw, imperfect data into trustworthy evidence you can explain.

modules.title: Rows, columns, and DataFrames
modules.mental_model: A DataFrame is like a spreadsheet with named columns, but Python can apply repeatable rules to every row.
evidence: explains what one row and one column represent
common_mistakes: assumes every column has the expected type
changes data without checking the result

modules.title: Load and inspect data
modules.mental_model: Loading data translates an external file into Python values; inspection checks whether that translation matches your expectations.
evidence: checks shape, columns, types, and sample rows
common_mistakes: loads real sensitive data into examples
understanding_checks: Which assumption did you verify first?
projects: load and profile a synthetic email-volume dataset

modules.title: Select and filter
modules.mental_model: Selection chooses which information to keep; filtering asks a yes-or-no question of every row.
evidence: filters rows and explains the condition
common_mistakes: confuses row filtering with column selection
understanding_checks: Which information did you intentionally remove?

modules.title: Clean and validate
modules.mental_model: Cleaning is not hiding bad data; it is making explicit decisions about missing, duplicated, or invalid values.
common_mistakes: drops missing rows without understanding why
fills missing values with an unjustified default
understanding_checks: What information could this cleaning step destroy?
projects: clean a deliberately messy synthetic dataset

modules.title: Group and summarize
modules.mental_model: Grouping creates buckets of related rows; aggregation turns each bucket into a useful summary.
evidence: chooses and explains a summary measure
common_mistakes: uses a mean when outliers make it misleading
understanding_checks: What does one output row represent now?
projects: summarize synthetic ticket volume by category

modules.title: Combine datasets
modules.mental_model: A join connects rows using a shared key; the join type decides which unmatched rows survive.
evidence: checks row counts before and after joining
understanding_checks: Which rows can fail to match?
Why did the row count change?
projects: combine synthetic tickets with a category reference table

modules.title: Visualize and communicate
modules.mental_model: A chart is an argument made with data; its form should make the intended comparison easy and honest.
evidence: chooses a chart for a stated question
common_mistakes: adds decoration that hides the comparison
understanding_checks: What question does this chart answer?
projects: create a short synthetic-data insight report
